proof.criterion: The round's one behaviour change: the block-id backfill's stored order replays to every version, and the order it replaced was wrong.
proof.surface: Go test against a real Postgres, driving the backfill over a room that holds a browser update the store has not taken yet: the browser appends a paragraph carrying the first block's id (so the document needs the repair that makes the backfill write at all), that append is held inside the store, and the backfill then stamps and stores
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<local Postgres> go test ./internal/dispatch/docs/ -run TestStoredOrderBackfillStampOverAnUnstoredEdit -count=1 -v (the test is packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/backfill_order_test.go, written by me this round)
proof.observed: PASS in 6.38s at 00441179: the backfill stamped, the held append was released, and CheckStoredOrder found no mismatch over a non-zero number of checked updates (the test fails if the check compared nothing).
proof.negativeControl: The same test against the previous head eb0fe0be, whose backfill appended its stamp alone (AppendUpdateTx with a class from closureChangedMarkdown, no flush): FAIL in 6.30s, `the stored history does not replay: pending update=2 parked_items=1 parked_delete_ranges=1` - the stamp was stored before the browser update it was made over, so the fold cannot apply it. So the old order was wrong, not merely different, and the test pins the new one.

proof.criterion: errForkReleased refuses as service-unavailable (503, retryable) rather than as an error that maps to 500.
proof.surface: Go test driving the real refusal on a warm room: one joined transaction appends, an operation is refused after it moved the fork so the fork is released, a browser edit the room commits moves it past the transaction's read point, and the transaction's next operation reaches rebuildFork's warm branch
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<local Postgres> go test ./internal/dispatch/docs/ -run TestAnEditWhoseForkWentAndWhoseRoomHasCommittedIsRefusedAsUnavailable -count=1 -v (the test is packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/fork_released_test.go, written for me this round)
proof.observed: PASS in 3.56s: the refused edit's error satisfies errors.Is(err, ErrServiceUnavailable), which is what api/server.go:636 maps to http.StatusServiceUnavailable. The test asserts the error a handler would map, not the sentinel's wiring, and it asserts on the way that it really released the fork (write.fork nil with updates already appended, write.cold false).
proof.negativeControl: Two temporary one-line changes to production code, each reverted and the test re-run green afterwards. Dropping the ErrServiceUnavailable wrap from errForkReleased (livewrite.go:378): FAIL, `the refused edit answered ... want the service-unavailable refusal a route serves as 503`. Replacing the warm-rebuild refusal at livewrite.go:408 with another error: FAIL with that error's text, which proves the test reaches that line and not some other 503 path.

backfillIsNotOnTheClusterPath: Read from the code, as the architect asked: Service.BackfillBlockIDs is called from packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/subcommands.go alone (lines 114 and 136, the backfill-block-ids subcommand, which builds a service of its own with no HTTP server), and nothing in internal/dispatch/api or the server's boot calls it. So a typed cluster load step never runs the backfill path, and no new cluster pass is owed for this change: round 3's cluster evidence stands (23 typed-document checks at the head, all clean, against a merge-base control mismatching on 5 of 6; dispatch://INFRA-707/artifact/infra-707-tester-cluster-passb-and-head-tar-gz).

The branch head 42677175 has no check run either.
ciAtTheHead.whatIDidAboutIt: My own push of this handoff carries NO skip-checks trailer, deliberately and against the usual rule for a handoff-only push, because it is the only push left in this round and it is what starts CI over this code. The reviewer must read the lanes at my push's head, which holds 00441179's code unchanged plus two test files and this handoff; a lane GitHub shows queued or running is read as such, and a red one sends the work back.
